findings.patch:
+++ b/django/db/models/query.py
@@ -1155,6 +1155,7 @@
 
     def first(self):
         """Return the first object of a query or None if no match is found.
+        Deprecated: Calling first() without explicit ordering will default to 'pk' ordering in Django 7.0.
         """
         if self.ordered:
             queryset = self
@@ -1168,6 +1169,7 @@

findings.description: New test cases in 'tests/get_earliest_or_latest/tests.py' lack comments explaining the purpose and expected outcomes of the tests.
findings.patch:

+++ b/tests/get_earliest_or_latest/tests.py
@@ -265,6 +265,16 @@ class TestFirstLast(TestCase):
         with self.assertRaisesMessage(TypeError, msg % "last"):
             qs.last()
 
+    """
+    Test the deprecation warnings for calling first() and last() after order_by() with no arguments.
+    - Verifies that a deprecation warning is raised for both first() and last() when called after an empty order_by().

findings.title: Test cases for explicit 'pk' ordering lack negative cases
findings.description: The tests added verify that explicit 'pk' ordering prevents the deprecation warning. However, there are no tests confirming that other field names or combinations of fields also prevent the warning, nor are there tests for cases where the warning should still be triggered despite ordering.

findings.title: No tests for concurrent access scenarios
findings.description: Given the nature of the changes affecting query ordering, there are no tests ensuring that the deprecation warning logic behaves correctly under concurrent access, which could be relevant for applications with high concurrency requirements.

findings.title: Lack of negative test cases for new warning logic
findings.description: The test suite additions focus on scenarios where the deprecation warning is expected to be triggered, but there are no explicit tests for verifying that the warning is not triggered inappropriately (e.g., when default ordering is set or arguments are passed to order_by()).

findings.title: Missing tests for edge cases in ordering logic
findings.description: There are no tests covering edge cases in the ordering logic, such as passing invalid field names to order_by(), or using complex expressions that might interact unexpectedly with the new deprecation warning logic.

findings.title: Tests do not cover all paths leading to deprecation warning
findings.description: The current tests do not cover all code paths that could lead to the deprecation warning being triggered, such as different combinations of ordered and default_ordering states.
